rule: Julia grammar validity vs Julia's own parser

oracle.kind: the language's own parser — an independent implementation
oracle.whyParseallNotParse: `Meta.parse` resolves operators in a single-expression scope and REJECTS `a +% b`; `Meta.parseall` accepts it, because Julia accumulates operator definitions across a toplevel sequence. An oracle built on `parse` would have reported the language's own wrapping-add operator as invalid — the same class of error as objc's edge audit calling a block parameter an unresolved target: the instrument's model reported as a fact about the product.
oracle.independence: shares no code, no grammar, no parse table and no data model with tree-sitter-julia. A truth file authored by the analyzer's own hand is a MIRROR by this repo's standard, which is why the yaml lane used PyYAML and why objc's F5 oracle cannot referee a grammar change at all.

scope: GRAMMAR VALIDITY ONLY. This is not a symbol or relationship differential — there is no analyzer yet, and a missing symbol is invisible to a parser-level oracle. It is stated here so the number is not read as more than it is.
